title: Non-Atomic Reference Clean-up with Concurrent Re-Acquisition
pattern: Using a simple increment/decrement atomic reference counter where a concurrent thread can increment the reference counter from zero.
why_bad: If a thread increments a reference counter that has already hit zero (but the object is not yet deleted), it will assume the object is live, while the releasing thread concurrently deletes the object, causing a fatal crash.
detection: Atomic increments on a reference counter that do not check if the current count is zero before incrementing (e.g. not using a compare-and-swap loop).
counterexample: Using `fetch_add_unless` or checking for zero atomically.
